title: Remove the dangling protocol data-files declaration from the platform wheel
summary: retire-the-agent-distribution-and-retired-protocol-surface deleted schemas/protocol and removed the protocol data-files entry from the root pyproject.toml, but packages/assayer-platform/pyproject.toml declared the same directory as "share/assayer/schemas/protocol" = ["../../schemas/protocol/*.json"]. That record's changedPaths did not cover the platform pyproject, so the declaration survived while its own forbiddenResponsibilities claimed no dangling reference to schemas/protocol would remain. The platform wheel is the distribution the install-matrix platform-only case installs, so the residue was on a real installed surface: building the wheel succeeds because setuptools silently ignores a glob whose directory is gone, and the wheel ships zero protocol entries while carrying the platform schemas, which is why nothing failed. This change removes that declaration, so the platform wheel no longer names a removed directory, and adds retirement notes and cleaned references to the documents that still described the removed surface: schemas/README.md linked the deleted envelope and tool-contract schemas, docs/tool-contracts.md linked them as well, docs/verification-and-traceability.md and docs/ws3-distribution-baseline.md cited them in their historical tables, and docs/architecture-governance-baseline.md, docs/platform-boundary-map.md, and docs/llm-agent-orchestration.md still described src/assayer_agent as present. Artifact content does not change, because no protocol entries were being packaged, so this is compatible rather than breaking. Verification evidence: the change landed in b67c0c1, pushed on 2026-09-17 with b67c0c1 as the publish point, and CI run 35202649162 passed all seven jobs including Install matrix at Python 3.11 and 3.13; locally the platform wheel builds without the declaration, the architecture check returns 0 on the repository and returns 1 when the retired declaration is planted back into packages/assayer-platform/pyproject.toml, the fast profile reported 444 tests OK and full reported 457 tests OK, and the design confirmation, architecture, document, plugin-source, English text, and resilience gates all returned 0.

platform: Release engineering owns every wheel's data-files declaration and the schema directory it ships
plugin: No plugin change; ordinary plugins are unaffected
agent: Documentation now states that the retired Agent loop is not present

forbiddenResponsibilities: No wheel in the repository may declare a data-files source that does not exist
No document may link or cite the retired protocol schemas as a current artifact
The change must not remove a schema, module, distribution, or entry that a live path uses
The change must not alter the platform wheel's remaining schema payload
acceptance: packages/assayer-platform/pyproject.toml declares no share/assayer/schemas/protocol entry and the platform wheel still carries the platform schemas
no file under schemas/ or docs/ links to schemas/protocol as an existing artifact
the design confirmation, architecture, document, plugin-source, English text, and resilience gates all return 0
the fast and full profiles still pass and the install-matrix platform-only case still installs and imports the platform

humanApproval.decision: Release-surface correction carried out under the standing authorization of the refactor mandate in #assayer-group:4c84ee19 and its delegation update, under which the agent and reviewer decide these changes themselves within at most seven workflow rounds. The classification is compatible because building the platform wheel already packaged zero protocol entries, so this removes a declaration rather than an artifact; @assayer_rev independently found the residue and proved that setuptools silently ignores the empty glob.
